valuation.method: Cyclical forward EPS x P/E. Earnings period priced at the Nov 2027 target date is FY2028 (year to Aug 2028), non-GAAP diluted EPS on about 1.15B diluted shares (company Q1 FY27 outlook basis), 15% tax rate (FY26 effective rate 14.8%). Anchors: FY26 non-GAAP EPS $75.52; Q4 FY26 EPS $33.42 at 87.0% gross margin; Q1 FY27 guide revenue $61.5B +/- $1.5B, gross margin ~86.25%, EPS $38.15 +/- $1.00. Base FY27 EPS is about $158 (four quarters near the Q1 guide) and FY28 normalises lower as DRAM pricing plateaus and supply (including CXMT and Micron's own $25B+ capex) grows. Multiples of 5.5-8.5x reflect peak-margin memory earnings, not a through-cycle P/E. Net cash $68.3B (about $59 per share) is not added separately; it is assumed to be embedded in the multiple. Model assumptions, not company guidance, beyond Q1 FY27.

bear.driver: DRAM/NAND price roll-over in 2027 as AI-capex digestion and new supply cut gross margin to about 60%

base.driver: Prices plateau after FY27; gross margin eases from about 86% toward 80%; revenue near FY27 level

bull.driver: Supply stays tight through 2028, HBM and server DRAM contracts hold margins above 85%, buybacks offset dilution

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY28 EPS of $140 the close implies 5.6x; the analyst-weighted target (about $1,700 from five named targets, mostly set before the early-November sell-off) implies about 12x on $140, or EPS of about $243 at 7x. At the Q1 FY27 guide annualised (about $153), the close is 5.1x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $140 (18.0 pp of the close); $10 of FY28 EPS moves it $70 (9.0 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Non-GAAP gross margin and DRAM contract pricing trend versus the 86.25% Q1 FY27 guide; a margin below about 80% would break the base case.
valuation.next_disclosure: Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings (quarter ends late November 2026; report expected in December 2026, date not confirmed in sources found).

analyst_notes: Named targets were set Sep 23-Oct 29, before the roughly 30% slide from Oct 29 to Nov 5 (reported close $656.39 on Nov 5), so every sampled target is stale relative to the price move; only Citi, Wedbush and Bernstein reaffirmed after the Q4 print. D.A. Davidson's $3,000 (19x FY27 EPS of about $158) dominates the spread; the other four cluster at $1,300-1,900. The gap to the base case is mostly multiple: analysts' targets need 10-12x on EPS near $140-160 versus 7x here. Five targets from six firms is a partial panel; published aggregate is $1,562 mean from 45-49 analysts (Yahoo/StockAnalysis).
